title: Yankees clinch playoff berth on September 15, securing third straight postseason appearance
dek: The Yankees defeated the Twins 8-3 on September 15, 2026, securing a playoff spot. It is their third consecutive postseason appearance and the eighth time in manager Aaron Boone's nine seasons that the team has reached October. Aaron Judge homered in his first game back from a three-month rib fracture injury.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The Yankees clinched a playoff berth by beating Minnesota 8-3 on September 15, marking their third straight postseason appearance.
bottom_line: The Yankees' path to the AL East title runs through four games against Tampa Bay beginning September 22 at home. Whether the club can close a 3 1/2-game gap in the season's final weeks will determine whether the postseason clinch signals a deep October run or a wild-card trajectory.
body: The Yankees clinched a playoff berth on September 15 by defeating the Twins 8-3 at Target Field in Minneapolis, according to MLB.com. The victory ensures their third consecutive postseason appearance and marks the eighth time in manager Aaron Boone's nine years at the helm that the team has reached October.

José Caballero homered and doubled in the clinching game. Aaron Judge hit his first home run since returning from the injured list, a three-run blast off A.J. Minter in the eighth inning that put the Yankees ahead 7-2. Judge had been sidelined for three months with a right rib fracture, per MLB.com reporting.
The Yankees overcame a 2-1 deficit with a six-run eighth inning, per the league's account. The game was played in constant drizzle at Target Field.

With the clinch secured, the Yankees now chase the AL East title against the Rays. According to MLB.com's reporting, Tampa Bay holds a 3 1/2-game lead over the Yankees, who stand at 87-63 with less than two weeks left in the regular season. The teams will play four games at Yankee Stadium starting on September 22.

Manager Aaron Boone told MLB.com the team developed "grit over the season" through "injuries, with adversity." The Yankees also called up 21-year-old George Lombard Jr. to play shortstop, per the reporting.
